title: Your First Batch File Line
body_md: Every batch file starts with **`@ECHO OFF`**. This hides the commands themselves from printing on screen—you only see the *output*. The **`@`** symbol hides even this line itself.

title: Printing and Comments
body_md: **`ECHO`** prints text to the screen—anything you write after it appears exactly as typed. **`REM`** creates a comment; the computer ignores everything after it. Use comments to explain your code.
code_snippet:
ECHO HELLO WORLD!!
REM This is a comment - totally ignored

title: Navigation and Control
body_md: **`CD`** changes your current directory (folder). Used alone, it shows *where you are*. **`cls`** clears the screen. **`PAUSE`** stops and waits for a keypress—keeps the window open so you can read output.

title: Copying Files
body_md: **`COPY source destination`** copies files. Use **`*`** as a wildcard (e.g., `*.txt` = all text files). When paths have **spaces**, wrap them in `"quotes"` or Windows breaks the command.

title: Deleting Files Safely
body_md: **`DEL`** removes files. The **`/s`** flag searches subfolders. The **`/p`** flag asks for confirmation *before each delete*—combine them for safe bulk deletion.

title: Moving and Renaming
body_md: **`MOVE source destination`** moves files (originals disappear, unlike COPY). Without a destination, it *renames* in place. You can move entire folders—if the destination doesn't exist, Windows creates it.

title: File Attributes
body_md: **`ATTRIB`** changes file properties. **`+r`** makes read-only, **`+h`** hides the file, **`-r`** or **`-h`** removes them. Combine multiple: `ATTRIB -h +r "file"` unhides *and* protects in one command.

title: Searching and Renaming
body_md: **`FIND "text" "filepath"`** searches inside a file and prints matching lines—both arguments need quotes. **`REN "full\path\old.txt" "new.txt"`** renames: first argument is the *full path*, second is *only the new name* (no path).
